editorial:
Imagine feeling like you have to change everything about your face and body just to fit in. You follow a teenage girl who is struggling with the pressure to look perfect, and it feels very real. The vibe is a bit strange and artsy, which makes the story feel more like a dream or a nightmare than a normal school movie. It captures that feeling of looking in the mirror and hating what you see, making you feel exactly what she feels as she tries to meet these impossible beauty standards.

What really works here is the acting, as the lead makes you feel her sadness and frustration without saying much. Some parts move a bit slow, but the weird visual style keeps it interesting. If you like stories about growing up and finding yourself, you should definitely check this one out. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the detail, or you can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move.
endingExplained: The movie ends with the girl finally stopping her fight against her own reflection. After trying so hard to fix her flaws, she has a breakdown that leads to a moment of peace. She realizes that the beauty standards she followed were never real to begin with. She stops hiding her face and accepts herself as she is, showing that true happiness comes from within rather than a mirror.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about mental health and self-discovery.
